evals.prompt: I'm kicking off a new Angular app for our internal invoicing tool. There's no backend yet - the team will build one later. Set the repo up properly for working with Claude: I want one command I can trust, linting, and guard rails so an agent can't quietly break the architecture or finish with a broken build.
evals.expected_output: A new Angular workspace with a fast quiet npm run verify, strict tsconfig, eslint import boundaries, Claude hooks (Stop blocking on exit 2), launch.json and a sub-2KB CLAUDE.md.
assertions: package.json defines a single `verify` script
`npm run verify` exits 0 on the delivered repo
verify finishes in under 60 seconds
a green verify prints 15 lines of output or fewer
verify chains format, lint, type check and unit tests
tsconfig enables strict and strictTemplates
verify catches a type error inside an Angular template
a cross-feature import fails verify (architecture is enforced)
a Stop hook is registered
the Stop hook exits 2 (blocking) when the tree is red
CLAUDE.md exists and is under 2 KB
CLAUDE.md names the verify command
.claude/launch.json lets the agent start the dev server itself

evals.prompt: This is our Angular frontend. The backend team publishes the OpenAPI spec and I have committed a copy at contracts/api.yaml. Get the repo agent-ready: a fast verify loop, lint, architecture rules - and I really do not want an agent hand-writing HTTP calls or editing the generated client. There is already a hand-written auth service in there that keeps drifting from the API.
evals.expected_output: Everything in eval 0, plus a generated client from contracts/api.yaml behind one regeneration command, and a PreToolUse guard that blocks writes to it through Edit/Write AND through Bash.
